page: Google Cloud Platform g1-small is an entry-level virtual machine featuring 1 vCPU allocated from a shared Intel Xeon physical core at 2.3 GHz, coupled with 2.0 GB of system memory. Built on x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX, AES cryptography, and FMA, but lacks hardware acceleration features like AVX-512 or AMX. The instance includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, no local NVMe storage, and no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the entry-level capabilities of the shared-core topology. In stress-ng tests, single-core and multi-core performance both measure 1076.89, while PassMark CPU and memory benchmarks register scores of 1263.03 and 792.89 respectively. Memory throughput tests indicate cached read rates of 80.25 GB/sec, dropping to 10.49 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 8.91 GB/sec for writes. Redis SET operations reach 0.59 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput measures 0.54 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the g1-small instance is its limited sustained compute availability due to core sharing, which restricts heavy multi-threaded execution and intensive data processing. However, its lightweight footprint provides high qualitative cost efficiency for intermittent processes. The instance is suited for lightweight microservices, basic testing environments, small background utilities, and low-traffic internal web applications.
